t.6.32.1: Then those rākṣasas, having gone there to Rāvaṇa's palace, reported that the city had been besieged by Rāma together with the vānaras.
t.6.32.2: Hearing that the city was besieged, the night-roamer was filled with rage; and hearing of the doubled arrangement of the forces, he ascended his palace.
t.6.32.3: He saw Laṅkā, with its mountains, woods and forests, surrounded on every side by countless troops of monkeys eager for battle.
t.6.32.4: Seeing the whole earth swallowed up, as it were, by the monkeys, he became absorbed in anxious thought: "How might they be destroyed?"
t.6.32.5: Having pondered for a very long time and summoned up his courage, the wide-eyed Rāvaṇa looked upon Rāghava and the troops of monkeys.
t.6.32.7: Those copper-faced ones, golden in hue, having given up their lives for Rāma's sake, advanced straight upon Laṅkā, with sāla trees, palms and rocks as their weapons.
t.6.32.6: Then, while the lord of the rākṣasas looked on, they climbed onto Laṅkā in those divisions, section by section, for the sake of doing what was dear to Rāghava.
t.6.32.8: With trees, with mountain peaks and with their fists, those monkeys smashed the lofty summits of the palaces and the arched gateways as well.
t.6.32.9: The monkeys filled up the moats, which were full of clear water, with dust and mountain peaks, with grass and with logs of wood.
t.6.32.10: Then the troop-leaders, some commanding troops of a thousand, some troops of ten million, and others accompanied by a billion, climbed up onto Laṅkā at that time.
t.6.32.11: The monkeys, crushing the golden archways and smashing the city gate-towers that gleamed like the peaks of Kailāsa,
t.6.32.12: Leaping up and bounding forward and roaring, the monkeys, resembling mighty elephants, advanced upon that Laṅkā.
t.6.32.13: Victorious is Rāma of surpassing strength, and Lakṣmaṇa of mighty strength; victorious is King Sugrīva, protected by Rāghava.
t.6.32.14: Proclaiming thus and roaring, the monkeys, who could take on any form at will, rushed toward the rampart of Laṅkā.
t.6.32.15: Vīrabāhu, Subāhu, and Nala, the forest-ranger, these leaders of the monkey troops, pressing hard upon the rampart, took up their positions there.
t.6.32.16: Meanwhile, they set up the encampment of the army.
t.6.32.17: The mighty Kumuda, surrounded by ten crores of monkeys who bore themselves as victors, blockaded the eastern gate and stood there.
t.6.32.18: Having reached the southern gate, the heroic and mighty monkey Śatabali, surrounded by twenty koṭis of monkeys, blockaded it and stood there.
t.6.32.19: Suṣeṇa, the mighty monkey, father of Tārā, went to the western gate and, surrounded by six hundred million monkeys, stood there besieging it.
t.6.32.20: Having reached the northern gate, the mighty Rāma, together with Saumitri, stood there besieging it, and so did Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys.
t.6.32.22: Dhūmra, the slayer of foes, of great valour, surrounded by a koṭi of bears of fearsome speed, stood at Rāma's side.
t.6.32.21: Gavākṣa the Golāṅgūla, huge of body, terrible to behold and of great valour, stood at Rāma's side, surrounded by a koṭi of monkeys.
t.6.32.23: Vibhīṣaṇa, of great valor and mighty strength, clad in armor and mace in hand, stood there surrounded by those ministers of his.
t.6.32.24: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha and Gandhamādana, running about on every side, protected the army of the monkeys.
t.6.32.25: Then Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, his mind seized by anger, swiftly ordered the march of all his forces at that time.
t.6.32.26: Then, urged on by Rāvaṇa, the soldiers rush forth in delight, like the surging waves of the great ocean as it swells at its appointed time.
t.6.32.27: Meanwhile a terrible battle broke out between the rākṣasas and the vānaras, like the war of the gods and asuras in former times.
t.6.32.28: Those terrible ones, proclaiming their own feats of valor, struck down the monkeys with blazing maces, with spears, pikes and battle-axes.
t.6.32.29: Likewise the huge-bodied vānaras, rushing forward impetuously, struck down those rākṣasas with trees and mountain peaks, and with their nails and teeth.
t.6.32.30: But other fearsome rākṣasas, stationed upon the rampart, tore apart those who stood on the ground with bhindipālas, swords and spears.
t.6.32.31: And the enraged monkeys too, standing on the ground, leapt up and, those leaping creatures, brought down the rākṣasas who stood upon the rampart.
t.6.32.32: That tumultuous clash between the Rākṣasas and the monkeys arose, a mire of flesh and blood, like a marvel to behold.
